+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import stat
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+SCRIPTS = ROOT / "scripts"
+if str(SCRIPTS) not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPTS))
+
+from code_lm_run_lock import release_run_lock, acquire_run_lock, lock_stale_after_seconds
+
+
+def _make_temp_lock(tmp_path: Path, *, stale: bool = False) -> tuple[int, Path]:
+    """Create a temporary run lock and return (fd, path)."""
+    # Ensure the directory exists
+    tmp_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    
+    # If there's already a lock file, remove it first so O_EXCL succeeds
+    lock_file = tmp_path / "run.lock"
+    if lock_file.exists():
+        lock_file.unlink()
+    
+    args = type("Args", (), {
+        "lock_path": "",
+        "rust_timeout_seconds": 0,
+        "public_timeout_seconds": 0,
+        "sts_timeout_seconds": 0,
+    })()
+    fd = acquire_run_lock(args, tmp_path)
+    if fd is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Failed to acquire lock")
+    return fd, lock_file
+
+
+def test_release_closes_fd_and_unlinks_same_path() -> None:
+    """Normal case: release closes fd and unlinks the same path."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_path = Path(td)
+        fd, lock_path = _make_temp_lock(tmp_path)
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+        assert not lock_path.exists()
+
+
+def test_release_does_not_unlink_different_path() -> None:
+    """Release should never unlink a different supplied lock path."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_base = Path(td)
+        # Create two distinct lock files
+        fd1, lock1 = _make_temp_lock(tmp_base)
+        fd2, lock2 = _make_temp_lock(tmp_base)
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd1, lock2)  # Wrong path
+            # lock2 should still exist; lock1 is closed but may or may not be unlinked
+            assert lock2.exists()
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd1)
+            os.close(fd2)
+
+
+def test_release_handles_already_closed_fd() -> None:
+    """Release should handle an already-closed fd gracefully."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_path = Path(td)
+        fd, lock_path = _make_temp_lock(tmp_path)
+        os.close(fd)  # Close before calling release
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        except OSError:
+            pytest.fail("release_run_lock raised OSError on already-closed fd")
+        # lock_path may or may not exist depending on whether it was unlinked
+
+
+def test_release_handles_stale_lock() -> None:
+    """Release should handle a stale lock (old mtime)."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_path = Path(td)
+        fd, lock_path = _make_temp_lock(tmp_path)
+        # Touch the lock to make it appear fresh
+        lock_path.touch()
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+        # Lock should be unlinked if stale_after is exceeded
+        assert not lock_path.exists()
+
+
+def test_release_preserves_replacement_lock() -> None:
+    """If path has been replaced, release should not unlink the new path."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_base = Path(td)
+        fd1, lock1 = _make_temp_lock(tmp_base)
+        # Replace lock1 with a new file
+        lock2 = tmp_base / "run.lock.new"
+        lock2.write_text("replaced\n")
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd1, lock2)  # Different inode than fd1
+            # lock2 should still exist
+            assert lock2.exists()
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd1)
+

+import pytest

+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+SCRIPTS = ROOT / "scripts"
+if str(SCRIPTS) not in sys.path:

+from code_lm_run_lock import release_run_lock, acquire_run_lock, lock_stale_after_seconds

+def _make_temp_lock(tmp_path: Path, *, stale: bool = False) -> tuple[int, Path]:
+    """Create a temporary run lock and return (fd, path)."""
+    # Ensure the directory exists
+    tmp_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    
+    # If there's already a lock file, remove it first so O_EXCL succeeds
+    lock_file = tmp_path / "run.lock"
+    if lock_file.exists():
+        lock_file.unlink()
+    
+    args = type("Args", (), {
+        "lock_path": "",
+        "rust_timeout_seconds": 0,
+        "public_timeout_seconds": 0,
+        "sts_timeout_seconds": 0,
+    })()
+    fd = acquire_run_lock(args, tmp_path)
+    if fd is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("Failed to acquire lock")
+    return fd, lock_file
+
+
+def test_release_closes_fd_and_unlinks_same_path() -> None:
+    """Normal case: release closes fd and unlinks the same path."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_path = Path(td)
+        fd, lock_path = _make_temp_lock(tmp_path)
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+        assert not lock_path.exists()
+
+
+def test_release_does_not_unlink_different_path() -> None:
+    """Release should never unlink a different supplied lock path."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_base = Path(td)
+        # Create two distinct lock files
+        fd1, lock1 = _make_temp_lock(tmp_base)
+        fd2, lock2 = _make_temp_lock(tmp_base)
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd1, lock2)  # Wrong path
+            # lock2 should still exist; lock1 is closed but may or may not be unlinked
+            assert lock2.exists()
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd1)
+            os.close(fd2)
+
+
+def test_release_handles_already_closed_fd() -> None:
+    """Release should handle an already-closed fd gracefully."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
+        tmp_path = Path(td)
+        fd, lock_path = _make_temp_lock(tmp_path)
+        os.close(fd)  # Close before calling release
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        except OSError:
+            pytest.fail("release_run_lock raised OSError on already-closed fd")
+        # lock_path may or may not exist depending on whether it was unlinked

+def test_release_handles_stale_lock() -> None:
+    """Release should handle a stale lock (old mtime)."""

+        # Touch the lock to make it appear fresh
+        lock_path.touch()
+        try:
+            release_run_lock(fd, lock_path)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+        # Lock should be unlinked if stale_after is exceeded
+        assert not lock_path.exists()

+def test_release_preserves_replacement_lock() -> None:
